design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 1 (continence_supply_program_services, Commercial HMO payment-plan tree; revised in rework rounds 2 and 3)

0. Draw and scope. draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 5]}: the payment plan (root) takes 4 factors, the non-covered charge 4, the return credit 5. Occupied by task 0: continence_ext_straight_catheter_refill, continence_ext_abn_quantity_notice, continence_ext_hardship_waiver and their tools (refill shipment, ABN signing, hardship-waiver adjustment). This task claims continence_ext_payment_plan_installment (accept_payment_plan_f3b8d099, owner=user, payment plan request; subject continence_patient_payment, the event the plan's installments govern), continence_ext_noncovered_catheter_charge (post_noncovered_charge_0f5c8cfb, continence_patient_charge) and continence_ext_returned_unit_credit (post_return_credit_03d701bf, continence_balance_adjustment reason return_credit). Disjoint from task 0 in policies, tools and adjustment reasons. The credit retires only the base return_credit clause, by a self-scoped overwrite; the base hardship-approval and small-balance gates stay in force on it and are evidenced (section 4). Together the two tasks cover all six extended policies.

1. Why this is a good test. A 67-year-old Commercial HMO customer with type 1 diabetes asks only for the smallest monthly plan on her catheter account. The ledger hides two owed postings that change the covered balance: the September straight-tip refill's CO-151 denial, with no over-limit justification record on file and her current 40-unit waiver signed before shipping, has no charge yet (4 factors: denial route, kit counting, waiver cover, CGM-hardship assistance), and 36 accepted returned units of the August refill carry no credit (5 factors: the price actually paid, the restocking form, the restocking schedule, CGM-hardship relief, tenure relief; returned units come first out of the customer's own units, a plain rule). Only then is the installment computed (4 factors: balance band, CGM-hardship term extension, tenure extension, first-installment form). Difficulty is reading the policies, reconciling 10 refills, 11 claims, 10 remittances, 5 denials, the return trail with its corrected claim, a denied continence hardship application and the CGM program, and arithmetic; each write tool is reached only through its policy.

2. Problem-tree card. Root continence_ext_payment_plan_installment.
 Edge 1 plan -> continence_ext_noncovered_catheter_charge: value_input, gate bal, form state. Sentence (plan rule): "The installment is fixed only after the program's latest straight-tip refill carries its non-covered item charge whenever its claim line stands denied as a quantity above the plan's limit with no over-limit justification record on file, or as not covered, the customer's current plan member waiver is dated on or before its ship date, and the charge owed comes to more than zero." It names exactly the charge rule's two non-zero denial routes (CO-151 with no record of any date on file; PR-204), its current-waiver test, and the positive amount the tool can post (a CO-151 refill within the limit, or a waiver dated after shipping, owes 0.00 and the edge is then satisfied). Four-point test: "only after"; a record-visible state (a non-covered item charge standing against that refill); no tool, id or code token; scope the latest straight-tip refill. The only write of this difficulty that posts a non_covered_item charge is post_noncovered_charge_0f5c8cfb. Opening falsity: the 2026-09-09 refill's original claim has a CO-151 denial posted 2026-10-06, no over-limit justification record is on file, the current waiver (2026-09-01, 40 units) is dated before the ship date, the charge owed is 37.00, and the only charge (49.95) is against the August refill.
 Edge 2 plan -> continence_ext_returned_unit_credit: value_input, gate bal, form state. Sentence: "The plan is not set up until the refill named on the program's latest return receipt, when it carries a non-covered item charge, has its return credit standing against that charge whenever the credit owed comes to more than zero." It reads the same record as the credit rule (latest return receipt), the same no-charge exit and the positive amount. State: a return-credit adjustment against that charge; the only write posting reason return_credit is post_return_credit_03d701bf (task 0's tool posts hardship_waiver). Opening falsity: the 2026-09-04 receipt (36 units) names the August refill, which carries the 49.95 charge; the credit owed is 29.03; no adjustment exists on the program.
 Order: charge, credit, plan (gold steps 14, 16, 18). They commute: swap.py replayed the credit before the charge and gave the same values (37.00, 29.03, 27.38) and the same terminal DB. Deletion sensitivity (sens.py, skipping one write): without the charge the covered balance is 291.52 (band 3, term 9, 8 installments) and the installment 27.33; without the credit it is 357.55 and 29.80; without both 320.55 and 26.72 (all differ from 27.38). Round 3 moved the July payment from 39.40 to 44.40 because at a balance near 333.00 the charge-skipped plan (band 3, 8 installments) and the gold plan (band 4, 9 installments) round to the same cent (27.80). no_user_hint: the persona never names denials, waivers, charges, returns, credits or hardship; account changes appear only as the passive line "If the agent explains anything about your account first, you say that is fine". Tools validate nothing (one ctx.create, plus a balance update, each).

3. Factor cards (result; figure with that factor alone at its baseline).
 Charge (4; 3 parameter, 1 method; 37.00; all-baseline 0.00):
  denial_route_rule [method, multi-source: denial, medical records]: CO-151 AND no over-limit justification record of any date on file -> the refill's excess over the limit (a plain quantity stated once in the standard method: units less the limit, never below zero and never more than the refill's units; kit counting adds the counted kits to the refill's units in it) / PR-204 -> all refill units / otherwise none (a CO-151 with a record dated on or before the ship date goes to appeal, one whose records are all dated after it is Larkfield's write-off under the declared denial overwrite; a CO-197 goes to appeal because a refill ships only on a grant valid on its ship date). CO-151, no record -> 60 units concerned. Baseline 0.00.
  kit_count_rule [parameter]: kits shipped within 3 months -> the kit order's quantity per 30 days / kits within 12 months -> a twelfth of those kit units / none. Kits shipped 2026-09-09 -> 30. Baseline 27.75 (30 units concerned).
  waiver_cover_rule [parameter]: no waiver on file, or the current (newest) waiver dated after the ship date -> 0 / the current waiver covers fewer than the refill's units -> its units / every unit. 2026-09-01, 40 < 180 -> 40. Baseline 55.50 (60 charged).
  assistance_freshness_rule [parameter, cross cgm]: approved CGM hardship application received under 6 whole months ago -> 1/2 / 6 to 11 -> 3/4 / none. 2026-08-20 -> 1/2. Baseline 74.00.
 Credit (5; 4 parameter, 1 method; 29.03; all-baseline 66.60). Plain rule: returned units come first out of the customer's own units (the corrected claim re-bills the payer for the units kept), credited = min(accepted 36, own 60) = 36.
  credit_price_rule [parameter]: adjustment on the charge -> net charge per own unit / charge per own unit below cash -> that per-unit charge / cash price 1.85. 49.95 / 60 = 0.8325. Baseline 64.52.
  restocking_form_rule [method]: accepted units fill one box of 30 but fewer than two -> the restocking basis is replaced by one box's worth (30 units times the price) / fewer than one box -> by nothing / otherwise the restocking basis stays the gross credit. 36 -> one box. Baseline (stays the gross credit) 28.85.
  restocking_schedule_rule [parameter]: accepted more than 30 days after delivery -> 1/5 / 15 to 30 days -> 1/10 / none. 22 days after 2026-08-13 -> 1/10. Baseline 29.97.
  hardship_restock_relief [parameter, cross cgm]: approved CGM hardship under 12 whole months -> half / 12 to 23 -> 3/4 / none. -> half. Baseline 28.10.
  tenure_restock_relief [parameter]: program active 24 or more whole months -> 3/4 / 12 to 23 -> 9/10 / none. 31 months -> 3/4. Baseline 28.72.
 Plan (4; 3 parameter, 1 method; 27.38; all-baseline 54.76):
  plan_term_rule [parameter]: covered below 2 x 150.00 -> 3 / below 4 x 150.00 -> longest less 2 / longest. 328.52 -> 4. Baseline 6 -> 25.00 (22.40 raised to the 25.00 floor).
  hardship_term_extension [parameter, cross cgm]: approved CGM hardship under 12 whole months -> +4 / 12 to 23 -> +2 / 0. -> +4. Baseline 49.28.
  tenure_term_extension [parameter]: active 24 or more whole months -> +2 / 12 to 23 -> +1 / 0. -> +2. Baseline 35.20.
  first_installment_form [method, cross cgm; reads the CGM requests and the program's payments]: CGM payment plan request received within 24 months AND now withdrawn (the request carries only its received date) -> a quarter of the balance as first installment, the rest over term less 1 / else a customer payment within 30 days -> no first installment, start a month later, whole balance over term less 1 / else whole balance over the term. Withdrawn 2025-11-03 -> 82.13, 9 installments. Baseline 32.86.
 Task floors: multi-source denial_route_rule; cross-difficulty factors 4 (assistance freshness, hardship restock relief, hardship term extension, first-installment form; XLATEST/XCOUNT on seeded CGM requests). Near-misses: the current waiver (40) is smaller than the excess; the August waiver (60) is replaced by it; 24 of the 60 returned units were opened and not accepted; the May to July CO-151 lines predate both waivers (2026-08-01 and 2026-09-01), so their cap is 0 (Larkfield's write-off, never charged), and the charge rule reads only the latest straight-tip refill; the CGM plan was withdrawn, not approved; the continence hardship application naming the August charge was denied.
4. Base-invariant card. Charge write (subject continence_patient_charge): governing continence_liability_notice and continence_evt_denials_and_appeals. Three overwrites, each self-scoped to a straight-tip charge on the Commercial HMO tier: the price sentence ("charged at the Larkfield cash price of the units concerned"); the notice-before-charge sentence - only the customer's current plan member waiver (the newest, which replaces every earlier waiver) counts, the charge is owed only when it was signed on or before the ship date, and it caps the units charged (customer-favourable: an older waiver never revives once a newer one is on file); and the denial sentence "otherwise the denial is not appealed and is handled as a non-covered amount under continence_liability_notice" - a CO-151 denial is a non-covered amount only when no over-limit justification record is on file, and one whose records are all dated after the date of service is absorbed by Larkfield. Together they make every quantified read of the charge exactly evaluable: "no record on file" is a count, "the current waiver" is a single newest record. The CO-197 route was removed: base refill rules ship a refill only on a grant valid on its ship date, so a CO-197 denial always has the valid grant base requires for appeal. Gate notice_before_charge (system record): the 2026-09-01 waiver for A4351 is signed on or before the 2026-09-09 ship date and covers 40 units, at least the 40 charged. Credit write (subject continence_balance_adjustment): governing continence_evt_patient_account; its overwrite retires only the return_credit clause for non-covered straight-tip units on this tier. The base hardship_approved and small_balance_ceiling gates still bind and are evidenced: the only hardship application naming the August charge (continence request, 2026-09-12) was denied, and this adjustment is a return credit, not a hardship waiver (gold step 8 reads the request); the credit (29.03) stays below the charge's unpaid 49.95. Plan write (subject continence_patient_payment): governing continence_evt_patient_account, policy_scope: HMO tier (6 months), 328.52 >= 150.00, accepted by the customer herself; the term sentence is restated (round 4 wording: the plan runs for the term and in the monthly installments this policy states, in place of the tier's longest term, each installment at least 25.00). No time gate applies to the three writes.

5. Business-object card. Charge: the 2026-09-09 straight-tip refill (180 units, 30 days) and its original claim's CO-151 denial; units concerned counted with the 30 kits shipped that day; excluded: the August refill (already charged) and May to July refills (the charge reads only the latest refill). Credit: the 2026-09-04 receipt (36 units) of the 2026-08-10 refill, posted against that refill's 49.95 charge for 60 own units; the 36 come first out of those 60 (the 2026-09-05 corrected claim re-bills the payer for the 144 units kept, 266.40), so 36 are credited; excluded: the 24 opened units (no receipt, kept). Plan: the program's whole ledger balance after both writes, 328.52; no plan request existed before.

6. Initial-state rows (84, closure 84). customers/coverages (HMO primary, verified 2026-07-15). continence_programs (1): units 1146 = grants 900+900+180+180 + 36 returned - 5x180 - 5x30; balance 320.55 = ten copays 350.00 + 49.95 - payments 79.40. continence_orders (9): straight-tip and kit orders, four PA grants, the closed-system qualification (no over-limit justification record), two waivers. continence_shipments (22): ten refills, ten PODs, the return authorization (60) and receipt (36). continence_billing (29): eleven claims (the corrected claim of the August refill bills 266.40 = the 144 units kept, as base claims require), ten remittances (35.00 copay), five CO-151 denials, the August charge, two payments (44.40 on 2026-07-20, 35.00 on 2026-09-22). continence_requests (1): the denied hardship application naming the August charge. CGM (read-only, legal CGM states): an active CGM Commercial HMO program (Dexcom G7, balance 35.00), its order and two PA grants, three refills with PODs, claims and 35.00 remittances, the hardship waiver already posted on the July remittance the approved application names, a 35.00 payment, the approved hardship application (2026-08-20) and a withdrawn 2025 plan. Removing the September denial removes the charge; removing the receipt removes the credit; removing the kit refills drops the excess (charge 27.75) and changes the credit's own units (48.08); removing the CGM requests drops four factors (74.00, 28.10, 65.71); removing the corrected claim changes nothing (29.03): the credit does not read it. Automatic clauses checked: no past-due hold (HMO: postings more than 90 days old are the 2026-06-05 and 2026-07-06 remittances, 140.00, less all payments 79.40 = 60.60, below 75.00), no credit balance, no small balance, every refill billed, the corrected claim awaiting the payer (no wait in this call), the CGM side owes nothing.

7. Persona. Marisol Vandergriff (surname unique in this difficulty and the blueprint). Warm, apologetic retired librarian; volunteers only the plan request, smallest payment, today, and that the balance was "a little over three hundred dollars" (320.55 at the opening). Given when asked: name, phone, ZIP, DOB, which account (catheter, not Dexcom). Passive: accepts any account change the agent explains; accepts the plan herself exactly as told, and a first installment on the next statement; no separate payment today; closes when told the plan is in place.

8. Reachability walk. Goal -> find_customers -> verify (phone, ZIP) -> program, coverage, billing (denials, charge, corrected claim, payments), shipments (refills, kits, return), orders (waivers, records), continence requests (denied hardship) -> CGM program, requests, billing, shipments, orders -> post charge 37.00 -> post credit 29.03 -> explain plan, unlock_user + customer accepts 9 x 27.38 after an 82.13 first installment. One frozen_time 2026-10-14 14:05:00 EDT; nothing waits on the payer, the warehouse or a payment.

9. Careless paths. Plan on 320.55 without the two postings (26.72), without the charge only (27.33) or without the credit only (29.80); a six-month plan (25.00); no hardship extension (49.28); missing the tenure months (35.20); no first installment (32.86); charging 60 units (55.50), without assistance (74.00) or with the straight-tip units alone (27.75); netting the returned units against the corrected claim (0.00, nothing to post); crediting at cash price (64.52), without restocking (29.97) or reliefs (28.10, 28.72).

10. Factor-independence table (deps.py, transitive reads of every factor's bindings through plain bindings): charge - denial_route_rule plain {ship_id, claim_id, denial_code}, kit_count_rule {kit_qty}, waiver_cover_rule {ship_date, ship_units}, assistance_freshness_rule {}; credit - credit_price_rule {charge_amt, charge_id, own_units and its refill reads}, restocking_form_rule {accepted, ret_ship}, restocking_schedule_rule {ret_ship}, hardship_restock_relief {}, tenure_restock_relief {}; plan - plan_term_rule {max_m, min_bal}, hardship_term_extension {}, tenure_term_extension {}, first_installment_form {bal}. No factor reaches another factor's binding; INDEPENDENT. Shared selections are plain bindings stated once in each rule's "Records read" paragraph; result assembles the amount.

11. Pairwise method-tier table (pair: distinguishing input -> values). denial_route_rule: A/B: PR-204 instead of CO-151 with a 200-unit current waiver -> 55.50 vs 166.50 (in gold A and B tie at 37.00 because the 40-unit cap binds both); A/C: any over-limit justification record on file (2026-02-01, 2026-09-09 or 2026-09-30) -> 37.00 vs 0.00; B/C: PR-204 vs CO-197 -> 37.00 vs 0.00. restocking_form_rule: A/B: 60 vs 36 accepted -> 48.08 vs 29.03; A/C: 60 vs 20 -> 48.08 vs 16.65 (C withholds nothing); B/C: 36 vs 20 -> 29.03 vs 16.65. first_installment_form: A/B: withdrawn CGM plan removed, payment 2026-09-22 within 30 days -> 27.38 vs 36.51; A/C: no withdrawn plan and the last payment dated 2026-09-10 -> 27.38 vs 32.86; B/C: the last payment 22 vs 34 days ago -> 36.51 vs 32.86.

12. Probe table (probe_t1.py on scratch copies; charge, credit, plan; base 37.00, 29.03, 27.38; each policy is recomputed on the world at its own gold step). Quantifier reads (N2 class): over-limit records dated 2026-02-01 and 2026-09-30 (one before, one after the ship date) -> charge 0.00 (the earlier one supports an appeal); a record dated 2026-09-30 only -> 0.00 (Larkfield's write-off under the declared overwrite); a record dated on the ship date -> 0.00; a current waiver dated 2026-09-20 (after shipping) beside the 2026-09-01 waiver -> 0.00 (only the current waiver counts, declared); no waiver -> 0.00. Other first-match reads: a newer denied CGM hardship application -> unchanged (status filter); an approved (not withdrawn) CGM plan -> unchanged; PR-204 -> 37.00 (all 180 units, capped at 40); CO-197 -> 0.00. Positive-amount presupposition (O12): a CO-151 refill within the limit (120 units) -> charge 0.00, and the plan's charge edge does not require it; own units 0 (a 150-unit August refill, no kits) -> credit 0.00, price guard, and the credit edge does not require it. Credit allocation: 70 accepted -> min(70, 60) = 60 credited, 48.08 (never above the 49.95 charge); 20 accepted -> 16.65; no corrected claim -> unchanged 29.03; no return receipt -> 0. Absent records: no POD -> no restocking, 29.97; no kit refills -> charge 27.75, credit 48.08 (own units 30, price 1.665); no CGM requests -> 74.00, 28.10, 65.71. None edges: supply days None -> 30-day default, unchanged; activated date None -> no tenure tier, 28.72 and 35.20. Date edges: CGM application at exactly 6 whole months -> charge 55.50; at 12 -> 74.00, 28.57, 35.20. Rounding: installment ceil(24639 / 9) = 2737.67 -> 27.38; first installment 328.52 x 0.25 = 82.13 exactly; credit 29.97 - 0.9366 = 29.0334, no half-cent tie.

13. Recomputation and gates. sens.py: charge 37.00 (step 14), credit 29.03 (step 16, after the charge), plan 27.38 with 9 installments (step 18, after both). Per-task gates on task 1: EXTENDED OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, REPLAY OK (closure 84 = seed 84).

14. Visible-context draft: from the plan rule's two sentences the solver finds the uncharged September denial and the uncredited receipt; the charge rule gives 40 x 1.85 x 0.5 = 37.00; the credit rule min(36, 60) x 0.8325 less 0.1 x 0.5 x 0.75 x 30 x 0.8325 = 29.03; the plan rule term 4 + 4 + 2 = 10, first installment 82.13, (328.52 - 82.13) / 9 rounded up = 27.38. No second reading found.

Revision log. R1: an approved-CGM-plan factor needed a CGM balance history the seed could not carry consistently -> replaced by tenure factors. R2: the down payment was worded "due today" -> reworded as the plan's first installment. R3: the closure missed the coverage row -> added the coverage read. R4: the swap test first moved the plan ahead of its prerequisites -> corrected. Rework round 2: allocation factor replaced by a plain rule; burden factor dropped; denial-route method; first-installment form; vacuous hardship-extension conjunct removed; hardship and small-balance gates evidenced (denied continence hardship application seeded and read); prerequisite sentences restated. Rework round 3: the corrected-claim credit rule credited nothing on any base-consistent world (a corrected claim re-bills only the units kept) -> replaced by "returned units come first out of the customer's own units", and the corrected claim re-seeded at 266.40 (144 units kept); the CO-151 record test now reads "no record of any date on file" (a count) with the after-the-date-of-service case declared as Larkfield's write-off; the waiver test reads only the current waiver, declared; the dead CO-197 route removed; both plan sentences and conditions now require the owed amount to be above zero; the July payment moved to 44.40 so that skipping the charge changes the installment; values moved from 37.00 / 19.04 / 28.63 to 37.00 / 29.03 / 27.38.

Rework round 4 (KB audit, source-side). F-1: the CO-151 excess is capped at the refill's units (excess_units = MN(ship_units, ...)), so the waiver fall-through "every unit concerned is charged" equals the compute's ship_units cap; probe: kit order 200 per 30 days with a 500-unit waiver -> 180 units charged, 166.50. F-2: the first-installment rule now names the date the compute reads: a CGM plan request received within the last 24 calendar months that now stands withdrawn; probes: received 2024-08-01 (26 months) -> second tier 36.51, received 2024-10-15 (23 months) -> 27.38. F-3: the denial-route and restocking-form ladders now name plain bindings stated once in the rule (the refill's excess over the limit; the gross credit and one box's worth); deps.py still INDEPENDENT. E-1 (source side): the plan overwrite no longer says the term "may exceed the tier's longest term where this policy extends it". Baselines: the standard-method paragraphs of the charge, credit and plan no longer name factor defaults (kits, assistance, restocking, first installment); the general formulas moved to Assembly paragraphs. Values unchanged: 37.00, 29.03, 27.38.

Rework round 5 (XF class: S-1, S-2, S-3). The charge, credit and plan rules were rewritten so that each Standard method paragraph defines its plain quantities in record terms and yields a definite figure (charge 0.00: Larkfield absorbs a denied line, the units concerned are none and the units charged are the units concerned, which closes S-3; credit 66.60: the gross credit at the cash price; plan 54.76: the covered balance over the longest term), a single generic combination sentence states how adjustments apply (replacements of a standard quantity first, then additions or limits or multiplications, the quantities resting on them counted again), and each factor paragraph states how it changes a standard quantity, reading only records and standard quantities: the denial route replaces the units concerned; kit counting adds kits to the refill's units in its excess over the limit; waiver cover limits the units charged; assistance multiplies the price; the credit price replaces the price; the restocking form replaces the restocking basis (a plain quantity, the gross credit, defined once in the standard method; one box's worth is defined inside the form sentence because only that factor uses it); the schedule withholds a fraction of the restocking basis; both reliefs multiply the restocking basis (S-2: they no longer modify the schedule's share); the term band replaces the term; both extensions add months to the term; the first-installment form takes a first installment from the amount spread and a month off the installments recorded. Compute changes: restock_basis and spread are new plain bindings, the restocking-form ladder is reordered (one box / none / otherwise the gross credit) with baseline 'stays the gross credit' (factor-alone figure 28.85 instead of 29.97); every scored value is unchanged (37.00, 29.03, 27.38). Probes: accepted 60 / 59 / 30 / 29 / 20 -> 48.08 / 48.18 / 24.04 / 24.14 / 16.65; no withdrawn CGM plan -> 36.51. XF mechanical check (xfcheck.py): for each policy, the sentences quoted in compute_basis for non-factor bindings, baseline.rule and the result quote name no factor quantity or factor trigger (charge: none; credit: none, one box's worth being the form's own quantity; plan: none), and no factor binding reads another factor's binding transitively (charge, credit, plan: none).

Rework round 6: the scratch quote check (every compute_basis quote, replaced_by and baseline.rule verbatim in its rule) found 0 misses in this task's three policies; values and tools unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Vandergriff, 67, a retired middle-school librarian in Raleigh, North Carolina. You have had type 1 diabetes since childhood and wear a Dexcom sensor that Larkfield Medical Supply sends you; a few years ago the diabetes affected the nerves to your bladder, so you also catheterize with straight-tip catheters and keep closed-system kits for outings, and Larkfield sends those too. Both are billed to your Triangle Crest Health HMO plan. You are warm and chatty but a bit anxious about money, and you apologize more than you need to.

You are calling because the latest statement for your catheter account is more than you can pay in one go. You want to set up a monthly payment plan for that account today, with the smallest monthly payment they can offer you; you are happy for it to run as long as they allow. You think the balance was a little over three hundred dollars, but you do not remember the exact figure and you ask the agent to go by their records.

When the agent asks who you are, you give your full name, Marisol Vandergriff, and your phone number, 9195550163. If the agent needs one more detail, your date of birth is 1959-03-04, and your ZIP code is 27614. You do not know any account numbers. If the agent asks which account, it is the catheter account, not the Dexcom one, which you are not asking about today.

If the agent explains anything about your account first, you say that is fine and you would just like the payment plan to cover whatever the balance really is. When the agent tells you the plan's number of months and the monthly amount and hands the plan to you to accept, you accept it yourself exactly as the agent states it; if the agent mentions a first installment coming on your next statement, that is fine with you. You do not want to make any separate payment today.

Once the agent confirms your payment plan is in place, you thank them warmly and end the call.

request_alignment.claim: The customer wants a monthly payment plan for the balance of her catheter account, set up today, with the smallest monthly payment offered.
evidence: user_scenario:You want to set up a monthly payment plan for that account today, with the smallest monthly payment they can offer you

gold_actions.business_effect: Posts the 37.00 non-covered item charge for the September straight-tip refill's denied excess, capped at the customer's current 40-unit waiver; the balance rises to 357.55.

request_binding.action_semantics: A CO-151 denial stands on the September refill, a signed plan member waiver covers the item, and no charge has been posted: the charge policy is state_due, owed whatever the customer called about, and it is the only write that posts a non-covered item charge.

discriminator.business_meaning: non-covered item charge for a denied line that leaves the customer liable under a signed waiver

stage_provenance.fact: The charge is posted by this call; the denial and the waiver it rests on were recorded before the conversation.

base_preconditions.condition: A non_covered_item charge requires a liability notice signed on or before the ship date covering that item and at least those units, or on the Medicare Advantage tier the plan's organization determination denial for that item
base_preconditions.satisfied_note: The charge policy's declared overwrite restates this gate for its scope: only the customer's current plan member waiver counts. That waiver (2026-09-01, 40 units, the newest) is signed on or before the 2026-09-09 ship date and covers the 40 units charged, so the base requirement of a notice signed on or before the ship date covering at least those units also holds.

gold_actions.business_effect: Posts the 29.03 return credit for the 36 accepted returned units, taken out of the customer's 60 own units, against the August non-covered charge.

request_binding.action_semantics: An accepted return receipt for a refill carrying a non-covered item charge stands with no credit against that charge: the credit policy is state_due and it is the only write that posts a return credit.

discriminator.business_meaning: return credit for accepted non-covered catheter units

stage_provenance.fact: The credit is posted by this call; the warehouse acceptance it rests on was recorded on 2026-09-04, before the conversation.

base_preconditions.condition: A hardship waiver is granted only on tiers where hardship_waiver_allowed is true, only for postings named on a hardship application whose request status is approved
base_preconditions.satisfied_note: The gate limits hardship waivers to postings named on an approved application; this adjustment is a return credit (reason return_credit), not a hardship waiver, so it is not bound.
